content.thinking:
I'm defining the blade geometry math—computing twist angle, width, and radius functions based on parameters along the blade's span.

I'm thinking through how to assemble the outer and inner edge points into a closed loop, handling the sharp tip and root corners, and checking that the curvature doesn't cause self-intersection near the tip. Now I'm working out the tapered width function for the edge strip, so it narrows smoothly to zero near the blade's root and tip.

Defining the spine ridge sweep...

Now I'm sketching coordinate conversion helpers for the SVG overlay and planning glyph outlines in unit coordinates for decorative strokes on the blade.

I'm figuring out the blade's overall dimensions and center position, deciding where overlay lines should sit relative to the bevel edges and blade tip, then moving on to coding the hub's gold plate and gem.

Setting up helper functions for the skull and jaw geometry, defining tilt angles and offset vectors to position points in 3D space, along with texture considerations for the blade and rune circle.

The hinge sits roughly aligned with the snout tip when projected forward along the jaw's angle, so the proportions check out reasonably well. I'm sketching the jaw ramus as a tapered box from the hinge point extending forward, shrinking in cross-section toward the tip.

Now I'm planning small decorative details: a painted bone texture with cracks, leather wrapping with lacing, and a teal-glowing gem decal near the forehead of the skull, positioned on the cranium surface for later fine-tuning. I'm also settling on the lathe helper's parameter order for building rotational shapes with bone attachment and spin.

For the floor clutter, I'm sketching out a femur-like capsule bone with knobbed ends, a small rib arc, and upright glowing teal shard cones scattered near the plinth, keeping everything within roughly a .95 radius so it still reads as part of the base composition. Time to actually write this out.
